messages:
Aisha: Quick weekly health check for Qorex onboarding (Mar 16-22). Focus: p95/p99 latency by route/model and streaming vs non-streaming. TL;DR: streaming p95 ~220ms (+8% vs last week), p99 ~620ms (+18%). non-streaming p95 ~340ms (-3%), p99 ~980ms (flat). Error rate bumped to 0.12% (mainly /chat-stream). Spend roughly flat.

Liam: Thanks — looking at the routing breakdown now. Dashboard: <https://redwood.prod/dash/qorex/latency?range=7d>

Marco: Confirming users saw slower responses yesterday evening around 20:30-21:15 UTC. One customer reported a failed stream that retried as sync.

Aisha: Noted. I pulled traces: most of the p99 tail for streaming is on model `mistral-7b-v2-stream` used by /chat-stream (longer prefix + tool calls). non-streaming traffic is mostly `llama13b-v2` on /complete.

Liam: Quick query I ran to reproduce numbers:

SELECT route, model, quant, percentile(latency_ms, 95) p95, percentile(latency_ms, 99) p99
FROM telemetry.requests
WHERE org = 'qorex' AND ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY route, model, quant
ORDER BY p99 DESC

Gives same pattern: streaming p99 concentrated on /chat-stream + tool calls.

CS-Bot: Incident created (#INC-512) — automatic alert for /chat-stream p99 > 600ms threshold.

Aisha: Root causes we suspect: 1) bursty long-context prompts hitting KV cache miss on one of the dedicated nodes; 2) occasional model kernel stall on the stream variant under high concurrency.

Liam: Concrete mitigations to try this week:
- Rotate a small percentage (10%) of /chat-stream to `mistral-7b-v2-sync` as fallback for >1024 token requests.
- Bump KV cache size on pool-7 for 24h and measure hit rate.
- Add adaptive batching cutover at 50ms queue threshold to avoid large super-batches during spikes.

Marco: That fallback would help our users — can you keep us posted on any UX impact? We don't want partial content truncation.

Aisha: Yep — fallback will switch to sync-only generation (no streaming chunks) for those requests; we'll watch completion time and error rate carefully. I'll run an internal canary: route-level config below:

route: /chat-stream
canary: {
  percent: 10,
  condition: request.tokens_est >= 1024
  fallback_model: mistral-7b-v2-sync
}
Expect to roll tomorrow 09:00 UTC for 2h canary.

Liam: Measured KV cache hit before change: 82% -> target >92% after bump. Also turning on quicker cache warming for repeated prefixes.

Aisha: Action items:
- Aisha: deploy canary + monitor p95/p99 and error rate (start 2432110800).
- Liam: increase KV cache and post metrics for hit-rate and tail latencies.
- Marco: coordinate with Qorex PM to notify end users about a brief behavior change if they hit fallback.

Marco: Will do. Also capturing customer feedback about content partials — they'll prefer consistent completions even if slightly slower.

Aisha: Noted. Follow-up check-in Friday morning to confirm whether tail improved. If p99 stays >600ms after mitigations, we'll escalate to infra for dedicated node repro / repro jobs. :thumbsup:

CS-Bot: Reminder — scheduled canary window (Aisha) on 2432110800.
